{{short description|French mathematician}}
'''Jean-Louis Nicolas''' is a French [[number theory|number theorist]].

He is the namesake (with [[Paul Erdős]]) of the [[Erdős–Nicolas number]]s,<ref>{{citation
 | last = De Koninck | first = Jean-Marie
 | isbn = 978-0-8218-4807-4
 | page = 141
 | title = Those Fascinating Numbers
 | year = 2009| publisher = American Mathematical Soc.
 }}</ref><ref>{{citation
|first1  = P. |last1 = Erdős | author1-link=Paul Erdős
|first2  = J.L. |last2 = Nicolas | author2-link=Jean-Louis Nicolas
|title   = Répartition des nombres superabondants
|journal = Bull. Soc. Math. France
|issue   = 103
|year    = 1975
|volume = 79 |pages   = 65–90
|doi = 10.24033/bsmf.1793 |url     = http://archive.numdam.org/article/BSMF_1975__103__65_0.pdf
|zbl=0306.10025
}}</ref> and was a frequent co-author of Erdős,<ref>[http://www.oakland.edu/enp/Erdos0p List of collaborators of Erdős by number of joint papers] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080804180523/http://www.oakland.edu/enp/Erdos0p |date=2008-08-04 }}, from the Erdős number project web site.</ref> who would take over the desk of Nicolas' wife Anne-Marie (also a mathematician) whenever he would visit.<ref name="sarkozy"/> Nicolas is also known for his research on [[integer partition]]s,<ref name="sarkozy">{{citation
 | last = Sárközy | first = A.
 | doi = 10.1007/s11139-005-0820-x
 | issue = 1–2
 | journal = The Ramanujan Journal
 | mr = 2166373
 | pages = 7–17
 | title = Jean-Louis Nicolas and the partitions
 | volume = 9
 | year = 2005| s2cid = 119401679
 }}.</ref> and for his unusual proof that there exist infinitely many ''n'' for which
:<math>\varphi(n) < e^{-\gamma}\frac  {n} {\log \log n} </math>
where <math>\varphi(n)</math> is [[Euler's totient function]] and γ is [[Euler's constant]]: he proved this bound unconditionally by providing two different proofs, one in the case that the [[Riemann hypothesis]] holds and another in the case that it fails.<ref>{{citation
  | last1 = Ribenboim  | first1 = Paulo | authorlink = Paulo Ribenboim
  | title = The New Book of Prime Number Records
  | publisher = [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]]
  | location = New York
  | page = 320
  | year = 1996
  | isbn = 0-387-94457-5}}.</ref>

Nicolas earned his Ph.D. in 1968 as a student of [[Charles Pisot]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=65866}}</ref> He works at [[Claude Bernard University Lyon 1]].<ref>[http://math.univ-lyon1.fr/~nicolas/ Jean-Louis Nicolas], [[Claude Bernard University Lyon 1]], retrieved 2015-01-13.</ref>

A conference in honor of Nicolas' 60th birthday was held on January 14–19, 2002 at the [[Centre International de Rencontres Mathématiques]] in [[Marseille]]. The proceedings of the conference were published as a [[festschrift]] in ''The Ramanujan Journal''.<ref>{{citation|title=Preface|journal=The Ramanujan Journal|volume=9|year=2005|issue=1–2|page=5|doi=10.1007/s11139-005-0819-3|doi-access=free}}.</ref>
